clue.text: Activity improving the mouth, long hair and eye, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of long hair and eye could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A list of grooming activities: tending one's long hair and perhaps one's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a joining word between the two stretches of fodder, which together hold exactly eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing and flossing are the routine care that keeps teeth and gums healthy, which is what this phrase names.

clue.text: After the accident, finally studied the tyre

indicators.note: finally here picks the closing letter of each of the three preceding words

parts.note: to have studied a text is to have read it

explanation.surface: After a car crash, someone finally got round to examining the damaged tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks as if it qualifies 'studied', but it works backwards on 'After the accident', giving R, E, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre given a new tread on its old casing is the remoulded kind, so the word can name the tyre itself.

clue.text: In tears all March, upset about end of February

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
upset signals that the letters of all March are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of February

explanation.surface: Someone has been crying all through March, distressed about the end of February.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL MARCH into LACHRMAL, and 'about' wraps that around Y, the last letter of February.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to weeping and the glands that produce tear fluid, so it describes something in tears.

clue.text: Fungus still besetting a section

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the first word encloses what follows

parts.note: still, as in 'still here', means yet
S is an abbreviation for section, as in legal references

explanation.surface: A mould is still attacking one section of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The organism used to raise bread and ferment beer is a single-celled kind of fungus.

clue.text: Carefully assess first of papers in entomologist's subject

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of papers inside the bug-scientist's subject

parts.note: an entomologist studies bugs and beetles, so the subject is an insect

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of papers

explanation.surface: A scientist scrutinises papers on bugs, the field of an entomologist.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely and critically is a direct synonym of the verb here.

clue.text: Centrally focused? It's scarcely different from not focused

indicators.note: scarcely different means only a slight rearrangement of letters, here the first two swapped

parts.note: something not in focus is blurred or unclear

explanation.surface: A wry remark that being focused on the centre is hardly different from being unfocused.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the opening U and N change places, which is why the clue says 'scarcely' different.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things relating to a nucleus, the central core, so it is playfully 'centrally focused'.

clue.text: Journalistic period that (paradoxically) could be so sane

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: a daft arrangement of the second word gives these two words

explanation.surface: A paradox: the frivolous news season could turn out to be perfectly sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: Treat the answer's first word as an anagram signal on its second: SEASON rearranged gives SO SANE, hence the paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet summer months, when newspapers fill pages with trivial stories, are known by this name.

clue.text: Sports handicap system: book is rather overlooking it

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the letters of it are left out

parts.note: rather, as in 'rather good', means quite
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports rule book seems rather to ignore the handicapping scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking it' removes IT from QUITE, leaving QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: In croquet, tennis and golf this is a free point or stroke a weaker player may claim, a form of handicap.

clue.text: I spot one about to swallow iodine — that's foolish

indicators.note: to swallow means the spot takes the chemical symbol inside it

parts.note: a spot is a dot
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
one as a Roman numeral is I
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone notices a person about to gulp down iodine and calls it stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idiotic is senseless or stupid, which is what foolish means.

clue.text: Son seen in a tie in part of Europe

indicators.note: seen in means the abbreviation for son appears inside the other pieces

parts.note: to lace is to tie, as with shoelaces
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy is spotted wearing a necktie somewhere on the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a region of north-eastern France bordering Germany, so it is one area of the continent.

clue.text: Criticise revered figure about subject of humour? It's how the distressed can respond

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: about means the revered figure wraps around the subject of humour

parts.note: an icon is a figure held in reverence
the butt of a joke is its target

explanation.surface: Mocking a sacred figure in comedy: a description of how upset people react.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in trouble presses an alarm switch that summons help, so it is the means by which they react.

clue.text: Drink line, one line not fully supplied by vintner, ultimately

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue
one as a Roman numeral is I

indicators.note: not fully means the word for a line is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of vintner

explanation.surface: A wine merchant has only partly stocked one line of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fully' trims QUEUE to QUEU, and 'ultimately' gives R from vintner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet, strongly flavoured spirit served after dinner is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Girl here is engaged in expression of gratitude

indicators.note: engaged in means the words here is are set inside the expression of thanks

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
here is contracts to here's

explanation.surface: A young woman has become engaged and is here, thanks be.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, so a fair crossword example of a girl.

clue.text: Drug source includes phosphorus

indicators.note: includes means the source word holds the chemical symbol within it

parts.note: a seed is the source of a plant
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A narcotic's origin turns out to contain a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphetamine is known by this slang name, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Satisfied a sailor is twisting bones

parts.note: to have met a demand is to have satisfied it
tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: twisting signals the word is turned round to run backwards

explanation.surface: A contented sailor is contorting his skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the five long bones of the foot between the ankle and toes, so a set of bones.

clue.text: 'Way to be followed is for every individual' — European leader

indicators.note: to be followed means the way comes first with the remaining pieces after it

parts.note: the Tao is the Way in Chinese philosophy
each means for every individual one

explanation.surface: A maxim, in quotation marks, that a philosophy applies to everyone, attributed to a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the Irish prime minister, the head of government of a European country.

clue.text: Animal's limb getting hurt in activity

parts.note: an arm is a limb

indicators.note: in means the word for hurt goes inside the word for activity

parts.note: ado is fuss or busy activity
ill means hurt or harmed

explanation.surface: A creature's leg is injured while it is busy doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Gangster family turning up: Italy soon almost devastated

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: fam is a common abbreviation for family
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: devastated signals the letters are wrecked into a new order
almost means the final letter of soon is dropped

explanation.surface: A crime family shows up, and Italy is soon nearly ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives MAF; 'almost' cuts soon to SOO, and 'devastated' rearranges I and SOO into IOSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Sicilian crime organisation is a gangster.

clue.text: Passed on segment of film scene giving nothing away

parts.note: passed on is a euphemism for died, so dead
a pan is a sweeping camera shot within a scene

explanation.surface: A dying moment in a film where the actor's face reveals nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face or delivery reveals no emotion, so it gives nothing away.

clue.text: Drink in cold bar initially providing limited comfort?

indicators.note: in means the drink goes between the two single letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of bar

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits in a chilly bar gives only a little consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a small crumb of comfort' means a tiny bit of consolation, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A way to block fuel from the shore

indicators.note: to block means sitting in the middle of the fuel word, obstructing it

parts.note: coal is a fuel
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A road is used to stop supplies of fuel arriving from the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or near the seaside, so from the shore.

clue.text: Hilltop plot covered in mud? Not at first

indicators.note: covered in means the plot sits inside what remains of the other word
not at first means the opening letter of mud is dropped

parts.note: a plan is a plot or scheme

explanation.surface: A plot of land on a hill turns out to be caked in mud, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes high ground, so it fits a hilltop used as a modifier.

clue.text: It's discourteous of female worker

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A remark that a woman employee is being rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque, casual manner that ignores politeness is rude, so it is discourteous.

clue.text: Daughter with little black anorak?

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
wee is Scottish for little
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a small dark waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is British slang for an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, not only a hooded jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a socially inept, obsessive nerd, so the second sense of the jacket fits.

clue.text: Mum's to dole out onion

parts.note: mum's the word means keep quiet, and sh is the call for silence
to allot is to dole out or distribute

explanation.surface: Mother is going to hand out the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: This small, mild bulb grown in clusters is a variety of onion.

clue.text: Item almost allowed after bold move

indicators.note: after means the trimmed word follows the bold move

parts.note: a coup is a bold, sudden stroke

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A thing is very nearly permitted after a daring manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' is the informal sense: two people in a relationship are 'an item'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically linked are called an item, which is a pair of partners.

clue.text: Merchant, one not taken aback in a negative response

indicators.note: in means the reversed words sit inside the negative response

parts.note: no is a negative answer

indicators.note: taken aback means read backwards

parts.note: one as a Roman numeral is I

explanation.surface: A trader who is not surprised when he gets a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice bears this name, so he is the merchant.

clue.text: Advance with titled lady, then stop, see

parts.note: a loan is an advance of money
a DBE, Dame Commander of the British Empire, is a woman with the title Dame
hold, as in 'hold it', means stop

explanation.surface: Someone takes out a loan with a dame, then pauses to look.
explanation.definitionFit: The old exclamation calls attention to something surprising, just like the imperative 'see!'.
